story.title: The Obituary Pilot
story.logline: A man who writes pre-written obituaries for healthy people realizes his own name just flashed on the assignment screen.
story.twist: The system doesn't predict death; it executes the writer's final keystroke.
story.ending: Who types the words when the typist is gone?

scenes.narration: Your death was scheduled for Tuesday at precisely noon, and I am the one who wrote it.
scenes.visual_prompt: A 28-year-old man with messy dark hair wearing a gray hoodie sits in a dark room lit only by a green glowing computer screen.
scenes.camera: Extreme close-up on his wide, terrified eyes reflecting text.

scenes.narration: Every morning, my newsroom terminal prints names of healthy people who will vanish before the week ends.
scenes.visual_prompt: A 28-year-old man with messy dark hair wearing a gray hoodie stares at a rolling text feed on a vintage amber monitor.

scenes.narration: We never question the system. We just describe how they fall, turning breathing souls into past tense.
scenes.visual_prompt: A 28-year-old man with messy dark hair wearing a gray hoodie frantically types on a mechanical keyboard with worn keycaps.
scenes.camera: Close-up on fast-moving fingers smashing keys.

scenes.narration: My editor says the ink is sacred. Once a draft is finalized, the universe clears its calendar.
scenes.visual_prompt: A 28-year-old man with messy dark hair wearing a gray hoodie pauses, staring at a red blinking warning box.
scenes.camera: Over-the-shoulder shot showing a warning popup.

scenes.narration: Today I sat down with my coffee, expecting a stranger's tragedy. Instead, my own keystrokes betrayed me.
scenes.visual_prompt: A 28-year-old man with messy dark hair wearing a gray hoodie reads his own full legal name scrolling onto the active draft line.
scenes.camera: Push in slowly on his trembling face.

scenes.narration: My address. My birthdate. Even the absurd detail about the chipped coffee mug sitting right beside my keyboard.
scenes.visual_prompt: A 28-year-old man with messy dark hair wearing a gray hoodie looks down at a chipped ceramic mug, then back to the monitor.
scenes.camera: Quick pan from mug to screen and back.

scenes.narration: If I delete the file, do I cheat the clock? Or does the empty screen mean the end comes faster?
scenes.visual_prompt: A 28-year-old man with messy dark hair wearing a gray hoodie hovers a trembling cursor over a giant red delete button.
scenes.camera: Macro shot of the mouse cursor shaking.

scenes.narration: My fingers refused to click. The cursor moved on its own, finishing the final sentence without my permission.
scenes.visual_prompt: A 28-year-old man with messy dark hair wearing a gray hoodie pulls his hands back in horror as keys click automatically.
scenes.camera: Low angle looking up at his terrified expression.

scenes.narration: The period at the end of my story flashed green. Outside my window, all the city streetlights suddenly died.
scenes.visual_prompt: A 28-year-old man with messy dark hair wearing a gray hoodie watches total darkness swallow the city skyline outside his apartment window.
scenes.camera: Wide shot from inside looking out at pitch black.

scenes.narration: The screen went dark except for one blinking cursor waiting for a new author. Who types the words now?
scenes.visual_prompt: A completely black screen with only a single blinking green cursor in the center.
scenes.camera: Static wide shot on the dead monitor.

caption.hook: He writes obituaries for the living.
caption.title: The Obituary Pilot
caption.caption: Arthur spent decades drafting final words for healthy strangers. But when his own name flashed on the screen, he realized the terrifying truth—the system doesn't predict death; it obeys his final keystroke. Would you finish the sentence?
